approach: vm sandbox loads index.html inline scripts (top-level var/function globals, no surgery); driver calls the engine's own init() (sandbox never fires DOMContentLoaded). Per level 0..29: startLevel(i) -> render() lays out state._grid; independent validation of the generated puzzle (proper 4-neighbor coloring, clues>0, clues prefilled); the board is played through the engine's own input path (longPressIdx=idx + handlePointerUp taps cycle each non-clue cell -1->0->..->nc-1->-1 to the generator's solution color); engine checkWin() -> setTimeout(doWin,200) must set screen='win', unhide #winScreen, persist best['L'+i] to localStorage sg_progress. Fairness audit on tiers 1-3 (<=6x6): independent solver counts clue-consistent proper colorings (cap 2).

results.persistence: sg_progress has best for all 30 levels

issues.rootCause: checkWin (index.html:540-547) requires EXACT equality playerGrid === puzzle.solution, but the generator (generatePuzzle, index.html:189-308) only guarantees the stored solution is A proper coloring consistent with the clues — it does no uniqueness check. Independent counting (cap 2) shows many levels admit >=2 valid colorings matching every clue: L1-L5 (4x4/nc3), L8-L10 (5x5) among tiers 1-3 alone (8 of the first 10 levels; larger tiers likely similar but were not counted for cost). A player who fills a different valid coloring — one that satisfies every visible clue and never triggers the adjacency-conflict feedback (sfxError at index.html:891) — can never win and gets no indication why.
issues.impact: Soft unfairness: unwinnable-from-valid-alternate-solution states with no feedback; player must backtracking-guess to find THE stored solution.
